meta.title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

activities.title: Refraction through a triangular glass prism
activities.summary: Trace light through a prism; mark angle of incidence, refraction, emergence, and angle of deviation.

activities.title: Dispersion of white light by a prism
activities.summary: Pass narrow white light through a prism onto a screen; observe the VIBGYOR spectrum band.

exercise_mcqs.question: The human eye can focus on objects at different distances by adjusting the focal length of the eye lens. This is due to
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Accommodation is the eye lens adjusting its focal length via ciliary muscles.

exercise_mcqs.question: The human eye forms the image of an object at its
exercise_mcqs.explanation: The eye lens focuses an inverted real image on the light-sensitive retina.

exercise_mcqs.question: The least distance of distinct vision for a young adult with normal vision is about
exercise_mcqs.explanation: The near point for a normal young adult is about 25 cm.

exercise_mcqs.question: The change in focal length of an eye lens is caused by the action of the
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens for accommodation.

intext_samples.question: A person with a myopic eye cannot see objects beyond 1.2 m distinctly. The corrective lens should be
intext_samples.explanation: Myopia is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens that shifts the image back onto the retina.

intext_samples.question: Fine particles in the atmosphere scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly. Which colour is scattered most, making the clear sky appear that colour?
intext_samples.explanation: Air molecules scatter blue light (shorter λ) more than red, so the sky looks blue.

intext_samples.question: Stars twinkle mainly because of
intext_samples.explanation: Changing refractive index of the atmosphere bends starlight slightly — the twinkling effect.

intext_samples.question: In a glass prism spectrum, the colour that deviates least is
intext_samples.explanation: Red light bends the least; violet bends the most in dispersion.
